title: Aqueous secretion and drainage
mechanism: Secretory epithelium supplies aqueous to a continuous anterior-segment route; outflow resistance helps determine pressure.

steps.title: Secretion
steps.explanation: Non-pigmented ciliary epithelium secretes aqueous into the small space behind iris and anterior to lens/zonules. Source capillaries, transporters and epithelial barrier are explanatory inset content, not resolved here.

steps.title: Through pupil
steps.explanation: Aqueous passes through the iris opening into anterior chamber. Pupil location marker stays hidden; fluid route must not pass through lens or vitreous.

steps.title: Conventional outflow
steps.explanation: At peripheral cornea-iris angle, aqueous traverses trabecular meshwork into Schlemm lumen. Collector channels and episcleral veins continue outflow outside supplied part inventory.

steps.title: Alternative route
steps.explanation: A separate textual branch explains unconventional outflow through ciliary muscle interstitium toward suprachoroidal/scleral pathways; do not route all fluid through Schlemm.

schematic_limitations: Static display is an ordered explanation, not simulated fluid dynamics.
Aqueous fills are content overlays; Schlemm is a thickened channel-location volume, not a resolved hollow wall.
No porous trabecular microstructure, pressure computation, fixed 85/15 percentage or validated flow speed.
Pathway arrows must be checked against built compartments before any future animation.

title: Tear film: secretion, spread and drainage
mechanism: Glands provide different tear-film components; blinking spreads film and aids drainage through medial puncta.

steps.title: Secretion to fornix
steps.explanation: Watery secretion passes through gland excretory ducts into superolateral conjunctival fornix. Expose the actual short ducts and host openings.

steps.title: Film and blink
steps.explanation: Blinking distributes a thin surface film across cornea. The surface step is not a solid duct bridging gland to puncta; film must remain external to globe.

steps.title: Distinct gland contribution
steps.explanation: Meibomian ducts open at lid margin and provide lipid. Conjunctival goblet cells contribute mucin but individual cells are not modeled. Neither gland system secretes intraocular aqueous.

steps.title: Medial drainage
steps.explanation: Upper/lower medial puncta take tears into canaliculi, then sac and nasolacrimal duct. Inferior nasal meatus is the off-model endpoint. Blinking aids drainage; do not prescribe a validated sac pressure cycle.

schematic_limitations: No tear film thickness or three discrete film-layer geometry is inferred.
The opened lid preset hides external covering; it is not physiological eyelid eversion or a blink motion.
Drainage mechanisms include multiple forces; no modeled valve dynamics, tear production rate or quantitative pump claim.
Inferior meatus and autonomic secretomotor pathway are unmodeled text endpoints.

title: Accommodation: distance to near
mechanism: Ciliary contraction reduces ring diameter and zonular tension, allowing lens/capsule reshaping to increase optical power.

steps.title: Distance state
steps.explanation: Conceptual distance state: relatively relaxed ciliary muscle, greater zonular tension, relatively flatter lens. Supplied static mesh is a reference shape, not a measured accommodative state.

steps.title: Ciliary contraction
steps.explanation: Parasympathetic input via CN III/ciliary ganglion activates muscle; ciliary ring narrows. Autonomic nerves/ganglion are unmodeled.

steps.title: Tension released
steps.explanation: Zonular tension decreases while fibres remain attached to ciliary region and capsule. Do not show active shortening of zonules or detach ends.

steps.title: Near state
steps.explanation: Lens axial thickness and curvature increase while equatorial diameter decreases; optical power rises. The capsule follows lens surface. Near miosis is related but must remain a separate pupil sequence.

schematic_limitations: Static steps explain causality without claiming mesh deformation.
Future morph needs coordinated lens/capsule, front/equatorial/back zonular attachments, iris/chambers and ciliary region; rigid scaling individual selectors is unacceptable.
Use qualitative changes initially; MRI cohort means are supporting observations, not template dimensions or per-diopter calibration.
No refractive-index field, refraction solver, binocular convergence or quantitative accommodation range.

title: Pupil control: light and dark
mechanism: Circular sphincter contraction reduces aperture; sympathetic radial dilator activity widens it.

steps.title: Bright light afferent
steps.explanation: Retinal activity reaches brainstem through CN II. Pretectal bilateral relays and Edinger-Westphal pathways are diagram/text context beyond this single eye.

steps.title: Constriction
steps.explanation: Parasympathetic CN III/ciliary ganglion/short ciliary pathway stimulates circular sphincter. Aperture decreases; iris remains rooted peripherally.

steps.title: Dark dilation
steps.explanation: Increased sympathetic radial dilator activity, with reduced parasympathetic constrictor activity, widens aperture. This is not the muscle mechanism of accommodation.

steps.title: Single-eye limitation
steps.explanation: Direct and consensual constriction require bilateral context. This right-eye geometry can depict only the local iris response; do not imply a second eye has been simulated.

schematic_limitations: Pupil is opening, never an opaque disk or tissue plate.
Future pupil motion requires iris surfaces, pigment epithelium, sphincter/dilator and chamber boundaries to update together.
No diagnostic reflex latency, pupil diameter, ganglion/neural circuit geometry or clinical examination claim.
Sphincter/dilator separate selectable meshes are representational subdivisions within iris.

title: Light into retina; neural signals out
mechanism: Optical transmission ends in phototransduction; neural processing then drives ganglion axons toward optic disc and CN II.

steps.title: Optical path
steps.explanation: Light crosses cornea, anterior aqueous, open pupil, lens and vitreous to retina. Posterior aqueous is a peripheral space behind iris, not a cavity that lies after lens along the central optical route.

steps.title: Retinal light depth
steps.explanation: In ordinary retina, incoming light crosses inner neural layers to photoreceptor outer segments beside RPE. At fovea inner layers are displaced; gross shell does not resolve these cells.

steps.title: Phototransduction
steps.explanation: Inset text: light reduces cGMP-gated inward current; photoreceptor hyperpolarizes and releases less glutamate. This is a graded response, not a photoreceptor action potential.

steps.title: Neural output
steps.explanation: Photoreceptor signals enter ON/OFF bipolar and interneuron networks; ganglion cells encode output in action potentials. Axons run in inner retinal nerve-fibre layer toward disc and exit through CN II. Neural arrows differ in color/style from optical rays; light does not travel down CN II.

schematic_limitations: Whole-eye neural shell represents a tissue compartment, not resolved synaptic circuitry. Link to separate retina model rather than rebuilding microanatomy.
Optical rays are explanatory overlays, not a ray-traced or quantitatively focused solution.
Do not animate all neurons as equally excited by light; ON/OFF pathways differ.
Optic disc lacks photoreceptors; do not terminate a focused optical ray there. Foveal and macular color patches stay optional location overlays.
